title: Frozen virtual call simulation
statement: Let $C$ be a finite Boolean Turing machine, with entry state $en$ and exit state $ex$, and let $arg$ and $result$ be Boolean words. Suppose that from the empty-input configuration with $arg$ on the designated state tape, $C$ reaches the corresponding configuration with state $ex$ and word $result$ after $t$ steps, and its state is never $ex$ at any earlier time. Then, for any Boolean input, valid input-head position, and output word, the virtual-head simulation started with tag true reaches after $t$ steps the corresponding configuration with word $result$, state $ex$, tag still true, and the same input-head position and output; it does not have state $(ex,true)$ at any earlier time.
hypotheses_covered: $C$ is a finite Boolean Turing machine
the base machine reaches its specified exit configuration after $t$ steps
the base machine does not have state $ex$ at any time $s<t$
$p$ is a valid input-head position for $x$
